title: Split-path SLI tagging and synthetic microbench for multi-region failover dashboards
creator: Dana Wong
description: Goal: Instrument request execution paths and build Grafana dashboards that surface split-path SLIs for real-time multi-region failover decisioning. We will tag telemetry at the request boundary to distinguish: fast-path (KV cache hit + compiled kernel), slow-path (KV miss, kernel fallback), retry-path (grpc retry + fallback model), and external-blocking (network/retry to storage). Dashboards should show per-region p50/p95/p99 for each path, kv-hit ratios, admission rates, circuit-breaker tripping counts, and shed events correlated with SLO breaches. Also add a synthetic microbenchmark harness that runs controlled traffic patterns (prefix-heavy, cold-cache, bursty) per-region to validate thresholds and automate playbook verification.
acceptance_criteria: Instrumentation: every request emits path_tag and kv_hit boolean with <1ms tagging overhead
Dashboards: Grafana panels for each region with p50/p95/p99 broken down by path_tag and tenant tier
Alerts: SLO alert rules for path-specific p95 crossing defined thresholds and automated pager/Slack routing
Synthetic harness: CI job that runs three scenarios (warm-cache steady, cold-cache spike, inter-region failover) and publishes baseline metrics
Playbook: documented automated failover steps (Confluence) linked from dashboard and validated by synthetic runs
